draft.title: Volume and capacity of prisms
card: A prism has the same cross-section all along its length. Its volume is the area of the cross-section \(\times\) the length.
Find the cross-section area first. For a triangle it is \(\frac{1}{2} \times\) base \(\times\) height, and for a rectangle it is width \(\times\) height.
Capacity is how much a container holds. \(1\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 mL, and \(1000\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 L. Also, \(1\text{ m}^{3}\) holds 1000 L.
Example: a tank has a rectangular cross-section of 20 cm by 10 cm and is 50 cm long. Volume \(= 200 \times 50 = 10{,}000\text{ cm}^{3}\), so its capacity is 10,000 mL, or 10 L.
draft.remember: Volume \(=\) cross-section area \(\times\) length. Then \(1000\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 L, and \(1\text{ m}^{3}\) holds 1000 L.

a.q: A prism is 10 cm long. Its cross-section is a triangle with base 6 cm and height 4 cm. Find the volume of the prism.
a.why: The triangle's area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12\text{ cm}^{2}\). The volume is \(12 \times 10 = 120\text{ cm}^{3}\). Using \(6 \times 4 = 24\text{ cm}^{2}\) for the triangle gives \(240\text{ cm}^{3}\), but that forgets the half.
a.clue: Find the area of the triangle first.

b.q: A rectangular fish tank is 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. When it is full, how many litres of water does it hold?
b.why: The volume is \(50 \times 30 \times 40 = 60{,}000\text{ cm}^{3}\). Since \(1000\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 L, the tank holds 60 L. Giving 60,000 L mixes up \(\text{cm}^{3}\) with litres, because 60,000 is the number of mL.
b.clue: Find the volume in \(\text{cm}^{3}\), then divide by 1000.
